newsitem.title: USA: HOTEL OWNERS ENJOINED FROM USING RITZ-CARLTON NAME.
newsitem.headline: HOTEL OWNERS ENJOINED FROM USING RITZ-CARLTON NAME.

text.p: The owners of four Ritz-Carlton hotels who filed a lawsuit against Marriott International Inc and Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co LLC have been enjoined from using the Ritz-Carlton trade name, said an opinion in the United States District Court.

District Judge John Martin of the Southern District Court in New York said in an opinion that the defendants are "enjoined from using the Ritz-Carlton trade name or any of its marks other than is incidental to their use."
Judge Martin added that the owners are also enjoined from using "such things as china, bath towels, door knobs, etc. that may bear the Ritz-Carlton name or logo."

Judge Martin concluded that if Marriott and the Ritz-Carlton LLC have wronfully terminated the management contracts of the four owners, then the owners will be entitled to recover any monetary damages they have suffered.

As previously reported, Ritz-Carlton LLC, which bestows its name on the hotels it is hired to run, pulled out of the hotels on August 2 and filed a lawsuit against Sheik Abdul Aziz Bin Ibrahim al Ibrahim's holding company, Al Anwa USA Inc, the owner of the hotels.
Ritz-Carlton alleged in its lawsuit that Al Anwa USA owed more than $4 million, meddled in the management of the properties and refused to make improvements to the hotels.
In its complaint, Ritz-Carlton LLC named as defendants N.Y. Overnight Partners LP, D.C. Overnight Partners LP, Savanah LP, New Remington Partners and an escrow agent, Mayer, Brown & Platt.
The owners of the hotels counter-sued Marriott and Ritz-Carlton LLC alleging fraudulent conveyance in connection with Marriott's 1995 acquisition of the hotel chain's assets.
Marriott owns a 49 percent stake in Ritz-Carlton LLC.
